messages.author: 7be55c8775cc3d7e
messages.subject: Setting Stan on AWS instance
parts:
I would like to share my own experience with STAN running on top of an AWS Linux instance, which I found very straightforward. 

First of all: The free-tier machine will kill the execution of basically any script. 

I'm not stating a general rule, but in my case I had a 2Mb environment and I installed rstan and its dependendencies (R will automatically take care of them) and another package xts (I didn't try without installing the latter, but I would reasonably say it's not there the issue). 

That's why I chose an M4-x machine to try my scripts (0.21$ per hour). 


sudo su     #so that I'll run everything as an admin

yum install -y R #to install R

#once installed

R

install.packages('rstan')  

#R will then ask you which CRAN mirror to use to install packages. Wait a couple of seconds and a list of countries with corresponding number will #appear, I had my machine in Northern California so I chose 50

q() #exit from R env

Rscript scriptom #scriptom is my script, in the same directory where I was in the cmd (otherwise specify path)





 



It's pretty simple, but it worked for me

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Setting Stan on AWS instance
parts:
Cool. Thanks. Stan needs a lot of memory to compile models, but
not nearly as much memory to run models. If you run in CmdStan rather
than R, the draws are streamed out and that really cuts down on the
amount of memory you need at run time.

So if you're using something like RStanArm, which pre-builds models,
then you should be able to get away with a smaller instance. You
might be able to do the same packaging in AWS.

- Bob
